title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Earlier pages define a 'carré' Q=(S,A,R): a combinatorial square with vertex set S, edge set A and set R of 'repères' (flags or frames). D is its symmetry group, dihedral of order 8. It has centre {1,ε}, where ε is the antipodism (rotation by π). Its three subgroups of index 2 are V_S (diagonal reflections together with 1 and ε), V_A (reflections in the axes through the midpoints of opposite sides, together with 1 and ε) and the cyclic group D^+. The three nontrivial cosets of the centre are C = V_S∖{1,ε} (the 2 diagonal reflections), D = V_A∖{1,ε} (the 2 axial reflections) and ω_Q = D^+∖{1,ε} (the two quarter-turns, i.e. the two orientations of Q). Each of these three sets is a Z/2-torsor under multiplication by ε. The page begins by listing these as canonical 2-element sets, together with the diagonals and the anti-diagonals.

Step 1: canonical bijections ω_S ≅ C and ω_A ≅ D. For the 4-element set S, the orientation (sign) torsor of S equals the orientation torsor of the 3-element set of its pair-partitions. This is because the sign map S_4→Z/2 factors through S_4→S_3. Equivalently it is the orientation torsor of V_S^* = V_S∖{1} = {ε}⊔C.

Step 2: the convention for orienting a 3-element set I in which one element a is distinguished (here a=ε). Choosing x in I∖{a} gives the cyclic order (a,x,y) with {y}=I∖{a,x}. Hence ω_{{a}⊔C} ≅ C, and so ω_S ≅ C. Likewise ω_A ≅ D.

Step 3: the 'remarkable relation' (*) ω_Q ∧ C ∧ D ≅ 1_{F_2}. This is a trivialisation of the contracted product of three Z/2-torsors. Reason: ω_Q, C, D are the preimages, in the central extension 1→{1,ε}→D→D_ab=F_2^2→0, of the three nonzero elements of D_ab, and these sum to zero. So for ϖ∈ω_Q, c∈C, d∈D the product ϖcd lies in the centre. Setting ϖ∧c∧d=0 ⇔ ϖcd=1 is compatible with replacing any one factor by its ε-translate. Equivalently, the structure group F_2^3 of ω_Q×C×D is reduced to the sum-zero hyperplane {x+y+z=0}.

Step 4: dependence on conventions. Since c and d anticommute modulo ε (dc = cdε), transposing two factors flips the trivialisation. Passing to the dual square Q' (vertices and edges exchanged, so C'=D, D'=C) gives ω_{Q'}∧C'∧D' = ω_Q∧D∧C. The resulting trivialisation is the opposite of that for Q.

Purpose. This is a careful, convention-tracking bookkeeping of the level-2 / Legendre-type symmetry (D_8 inside S_4 acting on 4 points). It prepares a canonical description of moduli of elliptic curves in characteristic ≠2. The next page identifies C×D with R/(antipodism) and ω_Q with the two orientation classes of repères.
errors: No mathematical error. The flip under transposition and under duality is correct: for a diagonal reflection c and an axial reflection d, cd is a quarter-turn and dc=(cd)^{-1}=cdε.
Minor gap: the bijection ω_S ≅ ω_{V_S^*} is asserted without stating the identification it uses. That identification is S_4 sign = S_3 sign via pair-partitions, i.e. the action of V_S on S.

ideas.what: Orientation torsor of a 4-element set identified with that of its 3 pair-partitions / of the nonzero elements of its Klein group
ideas.modern_name: sign character of S_4 factoring through S_4→S_3

ideas.what: Convention orienting a 3-element set with a marked point by choice of an element of the complement

Trivialisation ω_Q∧C∧D ≅ 1 from the three non-central cosets of D_8 over D_ab=F_2^2 whose sum is zero; reduction of structure group F_2^3 to the sum-zero hyperplane; sign depends on factor order (commutator pairing) and flips under square duality
ideas.modern_name: contracted product of Z/2-torsors from a central extension (commutator/Heisenberg-type pairing of D_8 as extension of F_2^2 by F_2)
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard group cohomology / theta-group formalism (Mumford for theta groups)

missed.claim: Viewed as a central extension of F_2^2 by F_2 with nondegenerate commutator, the dihedral group D of the 'carré' has the same shape as a level-2 Heisenberg/theta group of E[2]. The canonical trivialisation of ω_Q∧C∧D is then a torsor-level shadow of the theta-group commutator pairing (Weil pairing at level 2). Grothendieck does not make this link explicit on this page. It is a modest observation, not a new result.
missed.quote: les images inverses, dans l'extension D de D/{1,ε} = D_ab des trois éléments non nuls de D_ab
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: At most a pedagogical, convention-precise model of level-2 structures. A specialist would likely regard it as known.

deep.surprise_reason: Careful but elementary torsor bookkeeping for the dihedral group of order 8 and its cosets. It is typical of Grothendieck's convention-tracking in these notes, and none of the content is beyond standard knowledge.
transcription_corrections: 'Ens. des bijections canoniques' should read 'On a des bijections canoniques'.
'ensemble : deux élément' should read 'ensembles à deux éléments'.
'trois éléments (ici V_S^*)' should read 'un ensemble à trois éléments (ici V_S^*)'.
'en termes du choix d'un élément des complémentaires' should read 'en termes du choix d'un élément du complémentaire'.
'ω_S [?], C, D sont les images inverses' should read 'ω_Q, C, D sont les images inverses'. The relation concerns ω_Q, consistent with (*).
'dont la [?] {1,ε}' presumably reads 'dont la somme ... est nulle', i.e. the three nonzero elements of D_ab sum to 0.
In the margin, 'ω_S × C × D' should read 'ω_Q × C × D'.

'Attention, cette relation serait inversion' should read 'cette relation serait inversée si on faisait une transposition sur l'ordre des facteurs - il y a donc dans le choix de l'iso. une question de convention'.
The second displayed relation (ϖ∧c∧d=0 ⇔ ϖcd=1) is labelled (**), not (*).
